blocks.text: REACH.ai scans a salon’s live appointment book for last-minute openings and cancellations, then contacts the customers most likely to fill them, using machine learning.
The merchant dashboard was noisy and hard to trust during peak hours. As lead product designer, I redesigned it, from discovery to a design system.
The new dashboard doubled weekly engagement and cut support requests by 40%. Most clients on the old UI chose to upgrade.

items: Planned and led a 3-day onsite workshop in Phoenix, Arizona
Ran a heuristic evaluation of the existing dashboard
Gathered mixed-methods research from 52 customers through customer success calls
Designed the wireframes, the UI, and a design system

blocks.text: Owners needed a command center that made demand, staffing, and client conversations obvious at a glance. Instead, they juggled several tools in the middle of a packed Saturday.

blocks.quote: “I need an easy-to-use interface to gain quick, high-level insights into our client’s booking habits and how it affects our stylist’s schedule.”

groups.heading: Frustrations
items: Several complex communication tools
A noisy dashboard at peak hours
Appointment details spread across systems

groups.heading: Goals
items: Surface information to the owner on request
Fewer inbound calls and emails about bookings
Fewer front-desk interruptions

blocks.text: We couldn’t afford formal user testing, so customer success ran a mixed-methods study with 52 customers, asking the same three questions during sales and support calls. I then reviewed the existing designs against usability heuristics.

items: “There is a lot of information on the dashboard.”
“I can’t find what I’m looking for.”
“It’s difficult to change locations.”

image.alt: Annotated REACH.ai dashboard with heuristic findings

items: Simplify the color palette
Collapse redundant navigation into a calm primary rail
Optimize for mobile
Remove unnecessary and legacy features
Reduce the amount of content on the page
Establish consistent status color, type, and confirmation patterns

blocks.text: I planned and led a 3-day onsite workshop in Phoenix, Arizona to review the experience and find where to improve it. Activities included stakeholder alignment, research synthesis, dot voting, sketching, crazy-eights, critique, and a retro.

image.alt: Workshop participants reviewing sticky notes on a wall
Overlapping dashboard wireframes showing revenue overview and location selector

blocks.text: High-fidelity UI brought breathing room, confident typography, and a design system that made charts, status, and AI moments feel like one product.

items: Research without a budget: no formal user testing, so customer success asked 52 customers three questions and I added a heuristic evaluation.
Too much information: I simplified the palette, collapsed navigation, and removed legacy features.
Existing customers: the new dashboard had to be worth the switch, and most chose to upgrade.
